name: Elishama
overview: Elishama is a biblical figure associated with leadership and service in Israel, prominently identified as the son of Ammihud and prince of the tribe of Ephraim, who led and offered sacrifices for his people during the wilderness period (Numbers 1:10; 2:18; 7:48, 53; 10:22). Additionally, Elishama appears as a scribe serving in the royal court during the time of King Jehoiakim, highlighting a role of administrative responsibility and involvement in the governance of Judah (Jeremiah 36:12). These references collectively portray Elishama as a man entrusted with significant spiritual and civil duties within God's covenant community.
